title: Marketplace Entitlement Record
description: SSOT for the DATA shape of an entitlement — the record that an org MAY install/use a catalog listing. The marketplace agent WRITES it; the control-plane / storefront READ it to answer 'is this org entitled?'. DATA ONLY: it links to a purchase by an OPAQUE `purchase_ref` and carries NO Stripe/Connect/payout fields — the money system (owner-gated) lives outside this contract and joins in via `purchase_ref`. This is the who-owns-what record, not the payment. Revocation/expiry are first-class so the install/serve gate can fail-closed on a non-`active` entitlement.

entitlement_id.description: Stable, opaque entitlement id (unique per (org, entry) grant).

org_id.description: Opaque org id (optional; `org_slug` is the stable handle).

entry_id.description: The catalog entry id this entitlement grants (catalog-entry `id`).

kind.description: Artifact kind of the entitled listing.

source.description: Optional pinned gitea source-contract string of the entitled ref (the version the grant was made against).

status.description: Entitlement state. Only `active` authorizes install/serve; every other value MUST fail-closed at the gate.

granted_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp the entitlement was granted.

purchase_ref.description: Opaque link to the money system's purchase/subscription record. Carries NO card/Stripe data — it is a join key into the owner-gated payment layer, not payment data.

seat_limit.description: Optional seat/instance cap; 0 or absent = unlimited.

kind.description: Artifact kind. Same SSOT enum as catalog-entry.schema.json.

sourceRef.description: IMMUTABLE gitea source-contract string `gitea://<owner>/<repo>[/<subpath>]#<commit-sha>` — the `#ref` MUST be a FULL resolved commit SHA (40 hex for SHA-1, or 64 hex for SHA-256 repos) — never a short prefix (ambiguous as history grows), branch, or tag, NOT a branch or tag, so the install/authorization target cannot move under the org. The marketplace agent resolves a submitted tag to this SHA.
